method: tools/parity/oidc-differential.cjs against isolated copies of the API-initialized fixture, with one ephemeral local RS256 provider
normalization: Random UUIDs, access/refresh tokens, ID tokens, and timestamps are not retained; compare their semantic effects via selected user fields, redirect shape, and session count.
Node and Go use separate copied fixture directories and database files.
limits: Covered web auto-registration success, provider error, replay after provider error, and expired ID-token rejection.

Did not exercise authentication denial, existing-user linking, invalid signature/issuer/audience/nonce, mobile flow, expiry of in-memory flow state, callback cookies in detail, or Socket.IO user_added event recipients/payloads.
The report establishes only these four local mock-provider cases, not overall OIDC or identity parity.
